top_cited_works.title: Effect of fiber treatment on flexural properties of natural fiber reinforced composites: A review
top_cited_works.abstract: Fiber treatments and coupling agents have been applied by composites researchers to improve the functionality in the flexural loading of natural fiber reinforced composites. This paper reviews how fiber treatments upshot to flexural strength and modulus of natural fiber composites during 2000–2016. Chemical treatments improved fiber interface bonding with matrix and impart more strengths to composites. Coupling agents also ameliorate flexural properties and the combination of treatments is equally supercilious. The negative impact of fiber’s physical treatments on flexural properties of natural fiber composites also reviewed. Eventually, a number of perspectives have been concluded with the hope that our work will succor to further betterment in flexural strength of natural fiber composites.

recent_works.title: Scenario Based Assessment of Renewable Energy Growth Using LEAP Modeling for Sustainable Power Planning
recent_works.abstract: With the rising demand for electricity and growing worries about the environment, the need for sustainable electricity planning is imperative. The current paper proposes a scenario analysis on electricity generation in the state of Madhya Pradesh using the Long - range Energy Alternatives Planning (LEAP) model. The historical electricity generation pattern from the year 2004-05 to 2024-25 is studied and classified into the share of thermal, hydro and renewable electricity generation. The Business-as-usual (BAU) approach assumes the projection of electricity generation in the coming years using the linear trend approach from the period 2026-30. At the same time, an alternative approach is also designed in the research paper to demonstrate the effect of the rising share of renewable electricity on future electricity generation. The performance of the models is checked using statistical parameters like Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), the coefficient of determination (R2), and the correlation coefficient. recent_works.title: Physicochemical Monitoring of Food Waste Anaerobic Digestion
recent_works.abstract: This study investigates the use of anaerobic digestion to produce biogas from food waste collected from Hostel 9 at Maulana Azad National Institute of Technology in Bhopal. The mixed solid and liquid food waste was converted into a semi-solid substrate, which was then digested for 90 days in Up-flow Anaerobic Sludge Bed (UASB) reactor. The inoculum was cow dung, to which yeast and methanogens were added to enhance digestion. By examining important physicochemical parameters using accepted techniques, the process performance was analysed. The outcomes demonstrated improved effluent quality stabilization and efficient organic matter breakdown. This shows that food waste from hostels can be useful source for waste management and sustainable biogas production.

recent_works.title: Detecting and Adapting to Normality Shifts in Learning-Based Security Anomaly Detection
recent_works.abstract: Learning-based security applications are faced with many issues such as concept drift, which regularly leads to frustrations and decreased performance of the models as they get stale. It is a common assumption of these applications that both training and deployment models are identical, or the close-world assumption. Zero-positive anomaly detection is one of the most significant tasks in the security domains as it is resistant to the drift of abnormal behavior when trained without abnormal data. However, when normality shifts, this immunity results in more serious effects. The normality shift for zero-positive anomaly identification has received little attention in previous works, which have mostly concentrated on the drift concept of anomalous behavior. This paper promotes a general framework, to close this gap for deep learning-based anomaly detection in security applications. It recognizes, elaborates, and adjusts to normality shift in practice.
